output.brief: The remote promotion gap is mostly a difference in time in level, not in work location. Remote hiring only opened widely in July 2024, so 230 of 340 remote staff (68%) were under the policy's 18-month minimum at the census, against 200 of 760 office staff (26%). Among people who were eligible, remote and office staff were nominated and approved at nearly the same rates: 20.0% against 21.1% approved. That 1.1-point difference rests on only 110 remote staff and could be chance. Remote staff don't leave more often than office staff, and the gap appears in every job family, so job mix doesn't explain it. The evidence doesn't show that managers favour people they sit near. Some of your managers' comments hint at uneven access to urgent work, but nobody tracks that. I'm fairly confident, around 80%, in this overall picture. Don't announce the three-day office rule. It would penalize people hired on home-based contracts for a gap the data doesn't attribute to location. Instead, change the reporting to compare employees who were eligible under the policy, and re-check at the FY2027 cycle. Meanwhile, start tracking who gets stretch assignments, and clarify the promotion criteria for staff. The survey shows remote staff are less clear on how promotion works.
